title: Map the operating system
learning_outcome: Draw where the workflow runs, who approves it, and where evidence lives.
exercise: Place the job, decision, source, receipt, memory, and owner on one map.

boundaries.evidence: Use a generic stack; do not reveal Portfolio internal topology or credentials.
boundaries.privacy: synthetic Harbor only; no actual participant, client, admin, or private corpus content
boundaries.authority: prepare_only; no live agent, memory promotion, message, booking, spending, or publication

scenes.narration_exact: “Friday arrives at Harbor Learning Circle. Morgan has a draft Session Option Brief and a careful correction from last week. But imagine Morgan is out for an hour. Where is the brief? Which source note did the preparation role read? Who can answer a question about the unconfirmed facilitator? If the answer lives only in Morgan's head, our carefully designed pieces still do not make an operating system. We need one page that shows how the work travels.”
scenes.on_screen_copy_exact: “One request. One visible path.” “Where would a new teammate look?”
audience_copy: Where would a new teammate look?

scenes.narration_exact: “Chapter Eight gives the operating map five columns. Trigger: what actually starts this row? Role: who owns this step? Tier: what may that role do? Handoff: who receives the work next, including a refusal? Evidence: where can a human find the record? A blank is useful. If you cannot name the evidence location, write ‘missing.’ A tidy imaginary location would hide the work you still need to design.”

scenes.narration_exact: “The workbook also asks where approval, spend checks, public-safe proof, and rollback sit. This classroom workflow has no spending or public export. Mark those as closed paths with an owner, not as empty arrows that imply they might work. Rollback here means Morgan can withdraw a draft recommendation and record why. It does not undo an announcement, because no announcement happens. If your own paper map has a step without a named owner or a return path, circle it. That is the next design task.”

scenes.narration_exact: “Build the Operating Map in your Operating File. Use a fictional or approved example. Do not use private operational data. Give every row the five columns. Place the job, decision, source, receipt, memory proposal, and human owner. Label closed paths for spending, publication, and external messages. Then trace one failed source check: the note is stale, the draft stops, and Morgan receives a reason. We are making a design someone can review.”
scenes.on_screen_copy_exact: Exercise card below; 3:20 quiet writing timer with optional pause.
scenes.exercise_prompt_exact: Create an Operating Map with one row per step and columns `trigger | role | tier | handoff | evidence`. Mark where the L01 job, L02 Decision Card, L03 sources and receipt, and L04 pending memory proposal sit. Add explicit closed paths for spending, sending, publication, and live execution. Circle one missing owner or evidence location.
